submitter_note: Vaughn Jessome, constituency manager for the two Fort McMurray MLAs
community: First Nations and Métis settlements of northeastern Alberta (unnamed; '10 to 12 First Nations, two Métis settlements')
request: keep two rural-urban ridings for the Fort McMurray region (do not go back to one), because the rural-urban balance serves the area's First Nations and Métis communities
quote: I’m here to say that you can’t go away from the rural-urban setting, especially when you’re talking about First Nations, Métis, the rural communities that are there
note: General Indigenous-representation argument tied to a district arrangement (two rural-urban Fort McMurray ridings rather than one); names no specific reserve. Also confirms commissioner's statement that Gregoire Lake 176/176A is in Fort McMurray-Lac La Biche ('That's right'), a factual answer, not a request. Earlier statement at EB-343: 'two strong ridings that represent probably about 10 to 12 First Nations, two Métis settlements'.

submitter_note: Rene Wells, retired RCMP, Fort McMurray resident
note: Mentions Fort Chipewyan, Janvier as constituents/places; no district request for a reserve.

submitter_note: Angela Cobick, constituency manager, Peace River MLA
community: Woodland Cree, Lubicon, Kee Tas Kee Now Tribal Council nations (Loon Lake, Peerless Trout, Whitefish Lake/Atikameg); Little Red River Cree Nation
request: if Woodland Cree is moved into Peace River, Lubicon (and the other KTC nations) must come with it; prefers not to enlarge Peace River and, if it must grow, to add Berwyn and the rest of the MD of Peace instead; explains Little Red River Cree belongs in Peace River rather than Fort McMurray
quote: If we included Woodland Cree, you would have to include Lubicon
note: Answering Mr. Clark about the Peace River mayor's request to add Woodland Cree. Also says 'I’m not sure you can include one without including the rest' (KTC). Answers 'Yeah' to Clark: 'If we were doing one, we’d need to make sure we do both'. Little Red River Cree point (EB-355) is explanation of the current bump-out: 'it made more sense for them to be part of us rather than to stick them into Fort McMurray'. Berwyn alternative at end of record.

submitter_note: Carolyn Kolebaba, councillor, Northern Sunrise County
community: the five KTC First Nations (Woodland Cree, Lubicon and others)
request: do not move the five KTC First Nations into the Peace River riding (MLA cannot service them; riding is already too big)
quote: No. He can’t service them. Right now Scott Sinclair tries to get up there
note: Answers 'No' to Commissioner Samson: 'you’re in favour of the five First Nations being joined into the Peace River riding?'. Implies they stay in Lesser Slave Lake (Scott Sinclair's riding).

submitter_note: Gaylene Whitehead, councillor, Northern Sunrise County; lives at Cadotte Lake, says she represents the Cadotte Métis
community: Kee Tas Kee Now Tribal Council's five nations: Woodland Cree (Cadotte Lake), Lubicon, Loon Lake, Peerless Trout, Whitefish Lake (Atikameg)
request: move the five KTC First Nations (at least Woodland Cree and Lubicon, the closest) from Lesser Slave Lake into the Peace River riding, and keep the KTC nations together
quote: The only thing I would like to say about the boundaries is to include the five nations
note: Speaks as a county councillor. Self-identification ambiguous: says 'I represent the Cadotte Métis', that she earlier represented the Lubicon 'before they became a reserve', and speaks of 'our nations' and 'being a First Nation, they usually refer you to Grande Prairie'; coded member, could be nation_or_council or non_member. Answers 'Yes' to Clark: 'It would be important, then, to keep those together in one group.' When pressed by the Chair (EB-368): 'I suggested Woodland and Lubicon because they’re the closest to Peace River' and agrees to divide the five between the two ridings. Reason: Peace River is the shopping/service centre and the polling place First Nations would actually travel to.

submitter_note: Corinna Williams, reeve, Northern Sunrise County
community: Woodland Cree and the other KTC First Nations east of Peace River
request: do not bring Woodland Cree and the other KTC nations into the Peace River riding
quote: It would be too complicated with the four Indigenous representations that MLA Williams already has
note: Position shifts: first open to it only under 'a different configuration' not a bigger riding; answers 'I would say yeah' to the Chair's summary that the commission might 'bring in the county of Sunrise with those five First Nations'; then, after adjournment, reopens the record to say 'I don’t agree with that' and answers 'No' to 'You don’t agree with bringing them in?'. Final position coded.

submitter_note: Ken Vanderwell, vice-president, Lesser Slave Lake UCP constituency association; Slave Lake resident
community: the 11 First Nations of Lesser Slave Lake (Bigstone Cree, Driftpile, Kapawe'no, Loon River, Lubicon Lake, Peerless Trout, Sawridge, Sucker Creek, Swan River, Whitefish Lake, Woodland Cree) and the Métis settlements
request: keep Lesser Slave Lake whole so its First Nations and Métis settlements stay together in one district; if population must be added, go east
quote: The large population on reserves and settlements should not be split up as they identify with each other and the traditional areas they have lived on for generations
note: Also: 'Their interests and their influences are best suited and represented by a single representative at the Legislature' (54% Indigenous identity). Asks for section 15(2) special status. Suggests adding population to the east, noting the last commission added Calling Lake and communities 'with Aboriginal settlements on them'.
